title: A worker removed while films play costs no viewer a stall
description: Serves "Failures are invisible."; "Growing is adding machines.". An autoscaler removes workers without knowing which are busy, and a rolling upgrade stops every one. docs/transcoding.md says a worker that stops gracefully and is replaced within six seconds is not noticed; whether that holds for a worker that is removed and not replaced, with other workers already running, is unverified. PRODUCT.md: failures are invisible; the cluster can grow and shrink with demand by itself. D-045.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first, with real processes and the native browser check: a worker holding a watched re-encode, a watched copy, a helper and a subtitle extraction gets SIGTERM while another worker has room and no new worker starts. Recorded: what each viewer sees and the longest segment wait. If every criterion below already holds, only the checks and the docs land
From the signal the stopping worker claims no new job
With room on another worker: no segment request over 5 seconds, no dialog, the resume position kept; repeated 10 times in e2e with none failing
With no room on any other worker: what the viewer sees is measured and brought to the product owner as a brief before anything is built for it; it is never a stall without a reason
An interrupted extraction is taken up by another worker and no subtitle request is refused for it
The job's end is counted as interrupted and the log says the worker was stopping
docs/running.md gives the worker's termination grace and what it bounds
No start of play or seek is slower: time to first segment measured before and after
